MonitoringProgramDescription:
No one counts every visitor to the Tahoe Region, so visitation is read from the records that do exist: the room nights that hotels, motels, casinos, and vacation rentals report to the jurisdictions that tax them, and the visitor counts that parks keep at their gates.

Lodging records here run from 2018 to 2024 for the City of South Lake Tahoe, Placer County, Douglas County, and the Stateline casino core, and from 2019 for Washoe County. Sand Harbor visitor counts run from 2010 to 2022.
MonitoringApproach:
TRPA compiles lodging reports from the City of South Lake Tahoe, Placer County, Douglas County, the Reno-Sparks Convention and Visitors Authority (for Washoe County), and the Nevada Gaming Control Board (for the Stateline casino core). Each record is one area, lodging type, and reporting period, with the rooms available, the rooms rented, and the occupancy rate.

The reports are not alike. South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, Washoe County, and the casino core report by month, and Placer County reports by quarter. Washoe County reports rooms rented only, so it has no occupancy rate. El Dorado County outside the city is not in the table.

Sand Harbor visitor counts come from Nevada State Parks, by month. A season runs from May through April.
